title: Three telecom settlements and one tax account

beats.text: One phone tax lawsuit produced three San Francisco settlement ordinances.

visual.sub: Three settlement ordinances share one case number

beats.text: The claim alleged telecom providers had collected and sent in too little tax.

visual.kicker: Three settlement ordinances share one case number

beats.text: The AT&T group accounted for $15.4 million of the authorized settlements.

visual.kicker: Three settlement ordinances share one case number

beats.text: TPx accounted for $3.66 million. Four Verizon entities shared one $2.28 million amount.
Together the three amounts total $21.34 million.

visual.label: Three settlement ordinances share one case number

beats.text: In 2026, San Francisco changed how it counts internet phone connections.

visual.kicker: The later VoIP rule has its own starting date

beats.text: The new calculation depends on how many calls a subscriber can maintain at once.

visual.kicker: The later VoIP rule has its own starting date

beats.text: The Controller expected more than $20 million in one-time settlement payments.

visual.kicker: The Controller forecast payments from several payers

beats.text: Its $80 million forecast covered the whole tax account.

visual.label: The Controller forecast payments from several payers

beats.text: The current tax account later showed $79.60 million for the year.
The increase was close to the settlements, but the account does not identify the payers.
The transaction dates and the relator’s share still need a separate record.

visual.kicker: The tax ledger shows an increase but has no carrier breakdown

beats.text: A separate carrier, Bandwidth, deposited $3.8 million under protest in 2025.
Bandwidth sought a refund. Its October filing still disputed the assessment.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
